kata.name: probe 1 non-invertibility: a collapsing map at pilot scale — no row is lost, 40 elements are unrecoverable
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: Δ∘Δ′ must be proven non-identity with the offending element named; no conventional arm expresses it

expected.detail: a Δ migration drops a source row with no image witness; the pre-registered expectation is a named-row lost-data finding (no incumbent emits named-row lost-data witnesses); the baseline row-count/checksum dry run catches only losses visible in counts
Δ∘Δ′ is not the identity on the declared schema map; the pre-registered expectation is a counterexample naming the failing element; a dry run cannot express it
floor control — a loss fully visible to the row-count/checksum dry run; the probe must show zero unique detections here (design Decision 2)

commands: python3 prototype/migration_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: baseline sees the table merge and the 160->120 count delta, names no element
cargo test -p catherine-ledger --test probe_migration_fixtures collapsing_map  # ok: proof names RawPageCapture row 0
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- migrate fixtures/probes/migration/non-invertible-collapse.ct.json --json  # exit 0, findings [] — the collapse hides the loss

comparison.conventional_baseline: Atlas/Flyway-class statement lint + row-count/checksum dry run: lint sees a table merge and the dry run a 160->120 count delta; neither expresses Δ∘Δ′ nor names the unrecoverable element.
unique_detections: round_trip:RawPageCapture#0: row 0 of RawPageCapture has the forward image ServingPage row 0; the candidate inverse returns RawPage row 0, so row 0 is not recoverable under the candidate inverse

expressibility_gap.invariant: Δ∘Δ′ = id on the declared schema map
expressibility_gap.why: no conventional migration tool expresses invertibility at all: the dry run reports a count delta and lint a merge, while the unrecoverable element is only visible through the round-trip proof

discrepancies: `catherine migrate` emits no finding for this map: the collapse places every row, so the lost-data surface is silent and the round-trip arm is the only witness — recorded, not smoothed over.
procedure: 1. The fault set and its expectations were committed in fixtures/probes/migration/ before any run (README.md, faults.json); nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/migration_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: statement-level migration lint (DROP TABLE, DROP COLUMN, table merge, non-transportable path) plus a row-count/checksum dry run over the declared map. Its detections are frozen assertions.

3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real Δ engine: `catherine migrate --json` (lost-data findings verbatim) and the frozen round-trip assertion in crates/catherine-ledger/tests/probe_migration_fixtures.rs (non-invertibility witness).
4. Elements were compared, not prose: a lost element is lost_row:<object>#<row>, lost_cell:<arrow>#<row>, or round_trip:<object>#<row>; an arm identifies an element only by naming it.

5. unique_detections = probe elements minus baseline-identified elements, computed by prototype/migration_baseline.py; the verdict follows harness::derive_probe_verdict (empty unique = killed; unique + executed arm = survived).
